stories.headline: October inflation tops forecasts, raising bets on a December Fed rate hike
stories.summary: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than economists expected, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Tuesday. Treasury yields and the dollar rose and US stocks fell as traders bet the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates again in December. Fed official Waller plans to back at least a quarter-point increase, and Goldman Sachs added another hike to its forecast.
stories.why_it_matters: Prices for food, energy and housing are still climbing, and a further Fed hike would push up the cost of mortgages, car loans and credit card debt.
stories.background: The consumer price index is the government's monthly measure of what households pay for goods and services. The Federal Reserve raises its benchmark interest rate to slow borrowing and spending when inflation runs high; that rate stood at 3.88% this week, and a Reuters poll headline describes a December move as raising rates "once more". The Fed skipped a move in October, and a Reuters poll taken Oct. 16-20 found every economist surveyed expected an increase in December. The October report arrived shortly after midterm elections in which, The Guardian wrote, Republican losses were widely seen as a rebuke over high prices. The Fed's next decision comes in December.

facts.text: The consumer price index rose 0.4% from September to October, above economists' expectations.
The monthly increase was smaller than September's, and gasoline costs fell during October.
The AP reported that price increases extended beyond gasoline; PBS NewsHour said food and energy drove the rise and housing costs also went up.
PBS NewsHour said the country appears headed for an annual inflation rate of about 4% this year.
The Fed's Waller plans to support at least a quarter-point rate increase in December, Reuters reported.
The Fed's Paulson called for gradual rate increases, Reuters reported.
A Reuters poll of economists published Tuesday found they expect the Fed to raise rates in December.
Goldman Sachs added another rate increase to its Fed forecast after the report.
Treasury prices fell after the data; the Financial Times said two-year yields had their largest rise since 2024.
The dollar rose to a four-week high against a basket of currencies.
US stocks fell on Tuesday after the inflation report.

A larger move is on the table: The Washington Post's headline says a Trump-appointed Fed member signaled a big hike, and the Journal's currency report discusses pricing of a half-point move.

stories.headline: Lawmakers of both parties seek investigations of Nvidia chief over affair with suspected Chinese spy
stories.summary: Republicans and Democrats in Congress are calling for investigations into whether Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang compromised national security, after he acknowledged an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence has linked to China, The Hill reported. Nvidia has hired an outside law firm to investigate, President Trump said the FBI is looking into the matter, and shareholders have sued the company. Nvidia's shares fell on Monday and Tuesday and were rebounding early Wednesday, ahead of earnings due next week.
stories.why_it_matters: Nvidia is one of the most valuable companies in the world and a large holding in index funds and retirement accounts, so uncertainty about its leader reaches ordinary investors. The episode could also lead Congress to tighten the rules on selling advanced AI chips to China.
stories.background: Nvidia designs the chips that power most artificial-intelligence systems, and Jensen Huang co-founded the company and has run it since. The United States restricts sales of its most advanced chips to China on national security grounds, and Huang has lobbied President Trump to loosen those limits. Reports in The New York Times and the Financial Times connected a woman named Alice Huang, a former banker who worked for a company called Megaspeed, to Chinese intelligence; she is not related to Jensen Huang. On Sunday he acknowledged an affair with her, according to CNBC. Megaspeed is under U.S. investigation over alleged smuggling of Nvidia chips into China, which it denies, Deutsche Welle reported.

facts.text: Jensen Huang acknowledged on Sunday that he had an affair with a woman whom reports in The New York Times and the Financial Times connected to Chinese intelligence, CNBC reported.
Nvidia hired the law firm Wachtell Lipton to investigate; partner Joon H. Kim, a former acting U.S. attorney, is leading the inquiry.
President Trump said the FBI is investigating and that Huang told him he had "no idea she was a spy."
Republicans and Democrats are both calling for investigations but differ on whether the Trump administration is at fault, The Hill reported.
A shareholder lawsuit filed in California alleges Nvidia and Huang misled investors about the relationship.
A senior Republican on the Senate Banking Committee called on Huang to resign, Reuters reported.
Axios reported, citing multiple sources, that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick was sent a highly classified memo warning about the relationship.
The New York Times reported that Trump was reminded of intelligence about the relationship before Huang joined him on a trip to Beijing.
Lawmakers are pushing bills to restrict AI chip sales to China in response to the allegations.
Nvidia shares fell more than 4% on Monday, erasing about $200 billion in market value, and fell further on Tuesday; CNBC reported a rebound of about 5% on Wednesday.

The New York Times and Axios report that Trump and the commerce secretary were warned about the relationship beforehand.

stories.headline: CoreWeave results lift AI stocks after a month-long slide
stories.summary: Cloud-computing company CoreWeave reported third-quarter revenue above forecasts and raised its outlook, sending its shares up about 11% and lifting technology stock futures and European chipmakers on Wednesday. The rebound follows weeks of selling in artificial-intelligence stocks, including a further drop in Nvidia on Tuesday. Nvidia shares were up about 5% early Wednesday, CNBC reported.
stories.why_it_matters: AI companies make up a large share of the stock indexes held in retirement accounts, so swings in this group move many people's savings. The Nasdaq is down more than 8% over the past month.
stories.background: CoreWeave rents out data centers filled with AI chips and is one of several so-called neocloud companies that have borrowed heavily to expand. Investors have questioned this month whether spending on AI can be sustained, and CNBC reported that money has moved toward defensive sectors such as consumer staples and healthcare. Nvidia, the AI chipmaker, has been under separate pressure: its board opened an independent investigation on Nov. 8 after reports about chief executive Jensen Huang's relationship with an executive suspected of spying for China, and lawmakers from both parties have called for inquiries. Nvidia is due to report its own earnings soon.

stories.headline: Anthropic seeks a valuation above $1 trillion in its IPO
stories.summary: AI company Anthropic filed an amended registration statement for its initial public offering targeting a valuation of more than $1 trillion. Reported figures range from $1 trillion to $1.4 trillion, and the Financial Times reported that its bankers are preparing to raise the target to $1.5 trillion or more because of investor demand. Nvidia plans to invest $10 billion alongside the offering, The New York Times reported.
stories.why_it_matters: CNBC calls the offering historic in size, and its reception is being treated as a test of whether investors still want to pay high prices for AI companies, which weigh heavily in index funds.
stories.background: Anthropic is the company that makes the Claude AI models. A company going public files a document called an S-1 with the Securities and Exchange Commission that sets out its finances and, later, the price range for its shares. SiliconANGLE reported in September that a leaked filing showed an $8 billion operating loss alongside rapid revenue growth. The offering comes during a month-long sell-off in AI stocks and while Nvidia, a supplier and planned investor, faces investigations over its chief executive. Anthropic has also opened an offering to individual investors in Australia.

Reuters reported exclusively that the company is eyeing a $1.4 trillion valuation.

Nvidia planned to invest $10 billion alongside the offering, the largest of several new commitments from large companies, The New York Times reported.

Traders in perpetual futures are betting the shares will rise on their debut, CNBC reported.

stories.headline: Gasoline falls below $4 a gallon as oil retreats on Trump's Iran comments
stories.summary: The national average price of gasoline fell to $3.98 a gallon on Tuesday, according to AAA, the first time it has been under $4 since July. Oil dropped for two days, with Brent crude falling below $90 a barrel, after President Trump said the war with Iran was "effectively over" and pulled back from a threat of further strikes. Oil prices edged up again on Wednesday.
stories.why_it_matters: Cheaper fuel lowers costs for drivers and for shipping goods, though the October inflation report showed prices for other essentials still rising.
stories.background: Oil and fuel prices have been tied this year to the US conflict with Iran, and gasoline had been above $4 a gallon since July. Crude oil is the main input cost for gasoline, so pump prices tend to follow it with a delay. The Guardian reported that Brent crude, the international benchmark, fell to its lowest level since late August this week. The Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg reported that uncertainty over US-Iran negotiations is still supporting prices.

positions.claim: The New York Post's headline links the drop to Trump signaling no strikes on Iran soon.
